pr.title: Upgrade from the newest release's tag, check what it installed, and move v0 last
pr.head: 2920a3e5492a0781b9fbe538d415329d10d3059b

summary: project upgrade reinstalls Projector's CLI and each host's plugins by running install.sh, the same installer a first install pipes from https://projector.bot/install.sh. Until this change it fetched that installer, and the CLI's source archive, through v0: a tag every release moves, which projector.bot and GitHub each cache for about five minutes. Each host's plugin marketplace, meanwhile, follows the repository's default branch. So an upgrade during or just after a release could install a CLI from one release beside plugins from another, or run an older cached installer that never adds Codex's projector-hooks plugin, and still print success.
The change closes that gap in three ways:

1. Install from the release tag. upgrade asks GitHub for the newest release's tag, such as v0.9.0, and runs install.sh from that tag with PROJECTOR_REF set to it. A tag never moves, so no cache can serve an older copy. When the lookup fails, it warns once and runs v0's installer as before.
  2. Check what got installed. After a release install succeeds, upgrade runs that installer's own status and exits 1, naming the fix, when the CLI, a host's plugin, or projector-hooks does not match the release.
  3. Move v0 last. The Release workflow now publishes the GitHub release before it moves v0, so once v0 names a release, upgrade's lookup already finds that release.
Checkout installs, which run the checkout's own install.sh, and the plain curl | bash first install keep their behavior.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Release install. A CLI that pip recorded as installed from a release archive or a Git URL, rather than from a local checkout.
  • v0. The major tag every release force-moves. projector.bot serves install.sh from it.
  • releases/latest. GitHub's API for the newest published release, which never returns a draft or a pre-release.
  • status rows. Lines install.sh status prints, each a fixed-width name such as cli-stale followed by text.

groups.title: Find the release and fetch its installer
groups.kicker: How upgrade picks the tag it installs, and what it does when GitHub cannot say
intro: release_tag asks GitHub for the tag of the newest release in the repository the install came from. It tries a signed-in gh first, because that call does not count against the anonymous API's rate limit, and then the anonymous REST API through urllib. Each call has a 15-second timeout. A tag from either source must look like a plain tag name before it is used.

release_installer turns that tag into the URL of install.sh on raw.githubusercontent.com and sets PROJECTOR_REF for the installer, so the installer and the CLI archive it downloads come from the same tag. PROJECTOR_REF in your environment skips the lookup, PROJECTOR_REPO names the repository, and PROJECTOR_INSTALLER_URL still replaces the URL. After the installer succeeds, check_release reads the rows of its status to decide the exit.

checks.text: Every failure of the lookup, whether no network, a rate limit, malformed JSON, or a repository with no release, returns no tag and a reason. The upgrade then runs the v0 installer exactly as before, after one warning on stderr.

files.note: The lookup, the installer choice, and the check after the install, all on the release-install path of project upgrade.

checks.text: A tag must match [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*, so an API answer cannot add a path segment, a query, or a leading - to the raw URL. Checked by reading the regex and every use of the tag.

PROJECTOR_INSTALLER_URL replaces the URL but no longer skips the lookup, so the installer it names still gets PROJECTOR_REF set to the newest tag. test_an_installer_url_override_is_the_one_run pins that.

Rows are scoped by target: cli rows to the CLI, and plugin, hooks-, and host-missing rows to the host their text names. So project upgrade claude never fails over Codex, and a host that is not installed counts as checked. Traced against the row formats in install.sh.

The check runs only after the installer exits 0, and it runs the fetched installer's status, which asks the project on PATH for its version: the newly installed command, not this running process. Traced through report_cli.

groups.title: Two new rows in the installer's status
groups.kicker: The rows the check reads for Codex's hooks plugin and for a plugin ahead of its release
intro: install.sh status already compared the installed CLI and each host's projector plugin with the release's version. It gains two rows. hooks or hooks-absent reports whether Codex has the projector-hooks plugin, which carries Projector's hooks. plugin-ahead reports a plugin newer than the release, which is what the default-branch marketplace serves while a release publishes.

checks.text: plugin-ahead appears only without a checkout. A checkout's status still reports a newer plugin as plugin-stale.
Only the presence of projector-hooks is checked. Whether Codex trusts the hooks in /hooks is a step only a person can take, so it never fails the upgrade.

groups.title: Publish the GitHub release before moving v0
groups.kicker: The new order of the Release workflow's tag step, and how a re-run finishes it
intro: The Release workflow runs release.py tag after a version bump merges. It used to push the version tag, move v0, and then create the GitHub release. It now creates the release second and moves v0 last, and released lists what is missing in that order. Each step still runs only when the remote lacks it, so re-running a failed job finishes the release.

checks.text: Each partial state a failed run can leave is finished by a re-run: with the tag and no release, it publishes the release and then moves v0; with the tag and the release, it moves v0. In neither state does v0 name a version that releases/latest has not reached. Walked by reading tag, and covered by the reordered TagTests.

groups.title: Tests and documentation
groups.kicker: Fakes that keep the upgrade tests off the network, and the docs that describe the new behavior
intro: UpgradeTests now clears the three override variables, points PROJECTOR_GH_COMMAND at a fake gh, and serves the GitHub API from a temporary directory. The new UpgradeCheckTests run this branch's real install.sh status with fake curl, pipx, project, and hosts on PATH and a temporary HOME, so nothing reaches the network or the machine's own install.
